doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The IASJ and a career in education
title: Why he does his own bookings
summary: Nobody else can book his work as he does, and foreign promoters want to deal with Dave directly.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And there are very few people who do it well.

They don’t, and you end up doing it anyway. Michael told me something very interesting with his manager. He said it took five years. He said it ended up he had to teach him how to spell his name, because you can’t expect somebody else to read your mind. It’s understandable. I now – I have a quote. I have a manager now. But it’s impossible, because I – nobody can do it the way I’m doing it, because I do it for myself, and I’m first on the line to do it. Plus in our business, in a way, they want to talk to you. Now they know they can’t talk to Herbie or Wayne. That’s understandable. But Dave Liebman they can talk to, and they do not want to talk to – let’s say my wife did it, or you, being my representative. They want to talk to Dave, for whatever that’s worth. Not that I have wonderful discussions with a guy from Tallinn, Estonia, but it’s just that they want to be in touch with you, because they feel that too, especially the foreign thing, which is most of my work. They – to them, you are a legend, and they want to know that, “Dave, he answered me on line.” It sounds so dumb, but I know it means something, because I would have felt the same way if I was them. So there’s a lot of reasons why you got to do it yourself. That’s the way it is.
